metadata.case_name: LAU CHOW LAM v. FUNG MONG YAN AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: ironing worker in a garment factory
plaintiff.occupation_after: worked at home "disintegrating" woollen garments for about eight weeks (piecework)

injuries.description: The plaintiff had had a subtrochanteric fracture of the left femur. This had been operated on by the insertion of a nail in the neck of the femur secured by a plate on the shaft which was fixed with six bone screws. The fracture had firmly united but there had been over-riding of the two fragments resulting in a 3/4 inch shortening of the left leg. There was a loss of internal and external rotation of the legs of 20% each.

manifestations.description: a number of laceration scars on the face.
3/4 inch shortening of the left leg.
loss of internal and external rotation of the legs of 20% each.
would occasionally suffer from aches in the left hip and thigh especially in wet weather and during climatic changes.
used two crutches for two months and ever since then a walking stick.
7% impairment of the whole man (as assessed by Mr. R.G.M. Wedderburn, F.R.C.S.).
12% permanent disability (estimated by Mr. R.G.M. Wedderburn, F.R.C.S.).

treatments_received: insertion of a nail in the neck of the femur secured by a plate on the shaft which was fixed with six bone screws
use of two crutches for two months and thereafter a walking stick

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities (PSLA) - award under this head $35,000.

Loss of future earnings assessed at $138,000 due to inability to resume his job as an ironing worker (estimated loss of $1,150 per month for 10 years; potential earning capacity reduced to $850 per month from $2,000).
